solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: After removing cereal, wave bowl

indicators.note: after taking away says the cereal's letters come out of the longer word

parts.note: to wave a sword or stick about is to brandish it
bran is the husk of cereal grain

explanation.surface: Someone finishes their cereal and waves the empty breakfast bowl about.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is a shallow bowl for serving or eating food; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Commented about one chorus, taking up analytical approach

indicators.note: taking up, in a down entry, means the assembled letters are read from bottom to top
about means around, so the commented word goes round the next pieces

parts.note: to have commented is to have said something
I is the Roman numeral one
a chorus is a song sung by a group, or a refrain

explanation.surface: A critic's remarks on a choir piece adopt an analytical approach.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'taking up' means reading upwards, so the whole assembly is turned round after 'about' does its work.
explanation.definitionFit: Diagnosis is the analysis of symptoms or a problem to identify its cause, an analytical procedure.

clue.text: Is thus stimulated with a form of massage

indicators.note: stimulated means stirred up, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is so stimulated by a particular kind of massage.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiatsu is a Japanese therapy using finger pressure on points of the body, a type of massage.

clue.text: Crikey, so that's how envelopes are sealed?

definitions.meaning: an old northern English exclamation of surprise, like 'goodness me'

definitions.text: so that's how envelopes are sealed?
definitions.meaning: envelope flaps are stuck down by means of gum, read literally

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise on discovering how envelopes stick shut.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild Yorkshire-style oath of surprise; read literally, the phrase describes sealing with adhesive.

clue.text: They're drawn to effect changes in many a church

definitions.text: They're drawn to effect changes in many a church

parts.words: They're drawn to effect changes in many a church
parts.note: change-ringing produces sequences called changes on church bells, which ringers sound by pulling ropes, not by reforming the church

explanation.surface: Reads like reformers being drawn to change many churches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes' are ringing sequences, and 'drawn' means pulled, not attracted.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the cords hanging in a belfry that ringers pull to swing the bells.

clue.text: City that's as good in subdued light

indicators.note: in says the as-and-good letters sit inside the light word

parts.note: a glow is a soft, gentle light
taken as written

explanation.surface: A city said to look as good as ever in soft evening light.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasgow is Scotland's largest city, on the River Clyde.

clue.text: Mathematical operation commonly used in problem, on reflection

indicators.note: in says the popular word is placed inside the other
on reflection says the problem word is mirrored, read backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
something in widespread use or fashion is said to be in

explanation.surface: A mathematical operation commonly used in a problem, as one might decide on reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly used' looks like part of the definition; it gives IN, popular.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtraction is a basic arithmetic operation, named by the word for taking away.

clue.text: Hood to subdue bull, finally

parts.note: to cow someone is to intimidate or subdue them

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word bull

explanation.surface: A matador's or farmer's tactic: throw a hood over a bull to calm it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowl is a monk's hood, or a hood-shaped covering such as on a chimney.

clue.text: Cleansing tractor and front of heavy lorry

parts.note: a Cat is a Caterpillar tracked tractor

indicators.note: front of points to the opening letter of the word heavy

parts.note: an artic is British slang for an articulated lorry, a large truck with a separate cab

explanation.surface: A cleaning job involving a tractor and the front of a heavy lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathartic means purging or purifying, emotionally or as a laxative.

clue.text: Our group offering no light relief in film

parts.note: we refers to the speaker together with their group
someone stern is severe and humourless, giving no comic relief

explanation.surface: Our group complains that a film offered no light relief.
explanation.definitionFit: A Western is a film genre set in the American Old West, cowboys and frontier towns.

clue.text: Form of attraction having curious mammalian tinges?

indicators.note: curious as in odd or strange signals these letters are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wry question whether odd mammal-like colouring might be what makes someone attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal magnetism or charisma; also Mesmer's supposed hypnotic force, a kind of pull between people.

clue.text: New topic not opened for discussion

indicators.note: not opened says the word loses its front letter

parts.note: a matter is a subject or topic under consideration

explanation.surface: A meeting agenda item: a new topic that has not yet been opened for debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A natter is a casual chat or gossip, an informal discussion.

clue.text: Slight energy recalled regarding church service

parts.note: go means energy or vigour, as in 'full of go'

indicators.note: recalled, called back, says the words that follow are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: re means regarding or concerning
Mass is the Eucharist service in the Catholic church

explanation.surface: A recollection of feeling slightly energised by a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns RE plus MASS into SSAMER.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossamer means extremely light and flimsy, as an adjective close to slight or delicate.

clue.text: Silence surrounds rejected minion, mostly not a right-hand man?

indicators.note: surrounds says the silence word goes either side of the rejected word

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
rejected, as in thrown out, gives out

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a pawn is someone used by others, a minion

explanation.surface: A boss's servant is silenced and rejected for not being a proper right-hand man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right-hand man' usually means a trusted aide; here it is read literally as a right-handed person, which a left-handed boxer is not.
explanation.definitionFit: A southpaw is a left-handed person, especially a boxer leading with the right fist and punching with the left.

clue.text: Earl, say, and servant appearing in start of book?

parts.note: earl is an example of a noble title
a page is a boy servant or attendant

explanation.surface: An earl and his servant appear at the start of a historical novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The page near the front of a book bearing its name and author; the question mark flags a loose description.

clue.text: Surface exactly right in article

parts.note: off pat means known exactly, so pat means exactly right or apt
taken as written
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A finish or surface described as being just right in some article.
explanation.definitionFit: A patina is the sheen or film that forms on the surface of old bronze, wood or leather.

clue.text: Puritan so outraged about French writer

indicators.note: outraged suggests violent disturbance, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A puritan is so outraged by a French writer's racy work.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: 'about French writer' means of or relating to Proust.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective refers to Marcel Proust, author of In Search of Lost Time, so it means relating to him.

clue.text: Fancy I can block computer manufacturer supplying household gadget

indicators.note: to block is to sit in the way, so the shuffled letters go inside the manufacturer's name

parts.note: Apple is the Californian maker of Mac computers

indicators.note: fancy as in elaborate or fanciful signals a rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A boast that one can block a tech firm from supplying household gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb of desire but shuffles 'I can'; 'block' then lodges the result inside the firm's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance is a device such as a fridge or washing machine for domestic tasks.

clue.text: Figures securing University's position

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the figures word encloses the university letter

parts.note: stats is short for statistics, numerical figures
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Good figures have secured a university's standing in the league tables.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's standing or rank, a social or professional position.

clue.text: Tuck in with a beam after it finally appeared?

definitions.text: Tuck in with a beam after it finally appeared?

indicators.note: after places the eating and beam pieces behind that letter
finally points to the closing letter of the word it

parts.note: to tuck in is to eat heartily
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Hungry schoolchildren tuck in, beaming, once the food finally arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: the thing you tuck into, smiling, once it is brought in. Tuck is British school slang for snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A tray carrying afternoon refreshments, whose arrival invites diners to eat happily.

clue.text: Profit affected training centre

parts.note: boot is an old word for advantage or profit, surviving in 'to boot'
camp means exaggerated, theatrical, affected in manner

explanation.surface: A training centre's profits have been affected, perhaps by a downturn.
explanation.definitionFit: A boot camp is a training camp for military recruits, or an intense fitness course.

clue.text: Is copper in part of bridle coming to snap?

indicators.note: in says the earlier pieces go inside the bridle word

parts.note: the bit is the mouthpiece of a horse's bridle
taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A horse rider wonders whether copper in a bridle piece will snap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snap' looks like a verb; it is the noun, as in ginger snap.
explanation.definitionFit: A ginger snap is a crisp kind of cookie, so a snap is an example of the baked item.

clue.text: Rising quantity of hypochondria? I mean an actual disorder

indicators.note: Rising says the hidden letters are read backwards
quantity of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone clarifies that their rising hypochondria is in fact a genuine illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'actual' contrasts with hypochondria, an imagined illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A real medical condition: a deficiency of red blood cells or haemoglobin causing tiredness.

clue.text: French writer is after beer and tavern (in reverse order)

indicators.note: after places the word is behind the other pieces
in reverse order says the words beer and tavern are both written backwards together

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a bar is a drinking place, a tavern

explanation.surface: A French author's life, with beer and tavern visits in some order, as befits a bawdy writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in reverse order' turns ALE plus BAR into RABELA, which is followed by IS.
explanation.definitionFit: François Rabelais was the sixteenth-century French author of Gargantua and Pantagruel.

clue.text: Sailor getting on vessel, ousting one first in order

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor

indicators.note: ousting means throwing out, so that letter is removed from the vessel

parts.note: a boat is a vessel
a can stand for one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A sailor boards a boat and turfs out the first person in the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' means a religious order, not a sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbot heads a monastery, so he is the senior figure in a monastic order.

clue.text: Most of greens I'm turning over, finding sausage

indicators.note: most of says the final letter is dropped

parts.note: salad is a dish of green leaves

indicators.note: turning over says the letters of I'm are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A diner rejects most of the salad and turns to a sausage instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a highly seasoned cured Italian sausage.

clue.text: Version of marimba tune norm in popular song

indicators.note: a version is a reworking, so these letters are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: A marimba arrangement of a normal tune turns up in a pop song.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1965 Bob Dylan song, a hit for the Byrds, so a popular song by name.

clue.text: Instrument very likely to be recalled, in part

indicators.note: to be recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instrument is likely to be recalled by the maker, at least partly.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyre is a small harp-like stringed musical instrument of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Imposing figure cheers when coming into money

indicators.note: coming into says the thanks word goes inside the money word

parts.note: tin is old British slang for money
ta is an informal British thank-you, like cheers

explanation.surface: Cheers ring out as someone comes into a fortune and becomes an imposing figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a person of great stature or power, after the giant gods of Greek myth.

clue.text: Income that's not enough for some gambling

indicators.note: not enough says the word falls one letter short, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a wager is a bet, a piece of gambling

explanation.surface: A low earner laments that their income won't stretch to a flutter.
explanation.definitionFit: A wage is regular pay for work, a person's earnings or income.
